title: Introduction to Security
subtitle: Guess the hidden security terms — spin for consonants, buy vowels

puzzles.hint: A small buffer room between two locked doors that prevents tailgating
puzzles.explain: An access control vestibule (also called a mantrap) is a physical security control consisting of a small enclosure with two interlocking doors, ensuring only one person can pass through at a time. It prevents unauthorized individuals from following authorized personnel into a secured area.

puzzles.hint: Requires something you know, something you have, or something you are
puzzles.explain: Multifactor authentication (MFA) requires a user to present two or more distinct verification factors from different categories — knowledge, possession, or inherence — before granting access. This significantly reduces the risk of account compromise from stolen passwords alone.

puzzles.hint: Uses a matched public and private key pair to protect data
puzzles.explain: Asymmetric encryption uses two mathematically related keys: a public key to encrypt data and a private key to decrypt it. This model allows secure communication between parties who have never shared a secret in advance, and is the foundation of HTTPS and digital signatures.

puzzles.hint: Malicious code disguised as a legitimate or useful program
puzzles.explain: A Trojan horse is a type of malware that appears to be benign or useful software but contains hidden malicious functionality. Unlike a virus, it does not self-replicate; instead, it relies on the user to install and execute it.

puzzles.hint: A targeted deception attack crafted for a specific individual or organization
puzzles.explain: Spear phishing is a targeted form of phishing in which the attacker researches a specific victim and crafts a convincing, personalized message to trick them into revealing credentials or clicking a malicious link. It is far more effective than generic phishing because the content appears legitimate and relevant to the target.

puzzles.hint: A rogue wireless access point that impersonates a legitimate network
puzzles.explain: An evil twin attack involves an attacker setting up a fraudulent wireless access point that broadcasts the same network name (SSID) as a legitimate one, tricking nearby devices into connecting. Once connected, the attacker can intercept and inspect all network traffic passing through the rogue access point.

puzzles.hint: The systematic process of applying software updates to fix known vulnerabilities
puzzles.explain: Patch management is the practice of regularly identifying, acquiring, testing, and installing software patches and updates to operating systems and applications. Keeping systems patched closes known security vulnerabilities that attackers could otherwise exploit.

puzzles.hint: Centralized platform that enforces security policies on smartphones and tablets
puzzles.explain: Mobile Device Management (MDM) is a security solution that allows an organization to remotely configure, monitor, and enforce policies on employee mobile devices. Capabilities include enforcing encryption, requiring screen lock PINs, and remotely wiping a lost or stolen device.
